title: Emergent Pose-Invariance in 3D Molecular Representations via Multimodal Learning
experiments_summary: The study employs the following methods and experimental protocols: (1) Dataset curation: 855,000 molecules from PubChem were filtered by element type, heavy atom count, and charge. Each SMILES string was converted to 50 conformers via RDKit distance geometry and MMFF94 optimization, the five lowest-energy conformers were reoptimized using MINDO3 in PySCF, and the lowest-energy conformer was further evaluated at the RHF/STO-3G level. Electron densities were projected onto 128x128x128 voxel grids. (2) Model architecture: A 3DGrid-VQGAN adapted for volumetric inputs encodes electron density grids into quantized latents. The SMILES modality is encoded using the pretrained SMI-TED 289M transformer, which is fine-tuned during contrastive training. Two contrastive objectives are used: SMILESDFT-CLIP (symmetric InfoNCE loss) and SMILESDFT-SigLIP (sigmoid-based contrastive loss). Both encoders are trained jointly using AdamW (batch size 128, learning rate 3e-4, linear warmup over 1,000 steps, 50,000 total steps) on 4 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. (3) Retrieval benchmark: A benchmark of 1,000 molecules is constructed, each paired with five randomly rotated SO(3) variants. Rotation axes are sampled from six canonical directions and angles are drawn uniformly from [0, 360] degrees. Electron densities for rotated conformers are recomputed using RHF/STO-3G. Retrieval is evaluated in two settings: canonical (unrotated corpus) and unseen SO(3) rotation retrieval. Metrics include Accuracy@10, Recall@10, group-wise Recall@10 across six functional group classes, mean number of distinct rotational variants retrieved in top-10, and multi-pose retrieval rate. Comparisons are made against a unimodal 3DGrid-VQGAN baseline and the SE(3)-equivariant Pos-EGNN model. (4) Structure-property clustering: The latent space is analyzed for clustering of nitrogen-containing molecules by HOMO energy using the Davies-Bouldin (DB) index, without any quantum property supervision. (5) Downstream property prediction: Linear regression probes are trained on frozen pretrained embeddings to predict 12 molecular properties from the QM9 benchmark, reporting MAE on standard splits without fine-tuning the encoders.
